knowledge_units.context_summary: The density of states near the Fermi level in silver/magnesium oxide nanocomposites is dominated by nanoparticle states, suggesting DFT performance mirrors that of nanoparticles rather than bulk materials. Asymmetric inclusions like multi-layer disks exhibit dielectric enhancements exceeding 70%, surpassing expectations based solely on volume ratios. Local polarization fields show enhancement at nanoparticle poles and depolarization in equatorial regions, with the extent of these fields depending on inclusion shape and orientation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text outlines future research directions regarding ion distribution in supercooled droplets, specifically concerning Rayleigh fission and ion evaporation mechanisms. The study aims to serve as a foundation for analyzing low-temperature droplets containing peptides and ions to interpret ion mobility mass spectrometry data.

A library of 120 SiO2-supported catalysts containing ruthenium, tungsten, and phosphorus was tested for propylene oxidation. Key parameters identified for high yields of acrolein and acrylic acid include temperature, phosphorus content, and composition-weighted electronegativity.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study applies a subgroup-discovery (SGD) artificial intelligence approach to a hybrid dataset of high-throughput experimentation (HTE) and density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations to identify design rules for selective oxidation catalysts. The method focuses on local behaviors by selecting subgroups of materials with outstanding target values, specifically the yield of oxygenates in propylene oxidation, rather than modeling the full catalytic progression globally.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates 120 SiO2-supported catalysts composed of ruthenium, tungsten, and phosphorus for the selective oxidation of propylene. Reactions were conducted in fixed-bed reactors at temperatures between 200 and 400 degrees Celsius, with a fixed catalyst mass to maintain constant contact time. The catalysts are characterized by their composition rather than crystallinity, as similar performance was observed in both crystalline and disordered phases.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study validates subgroup discovery (SGD) rules for designing four- and five-component catalysts, showing that these complex materials achieve oxygenate yields up to twice those of the three-component training set. The highest performing four-component catalyst contains tellurium, while the best five-component catalyst contains tantalum, both operating at 400°C. A new SGD analysis of the expanded dataset identifies higher temperature and different composition parameters as key for this complex material class.

These rules indicate that higher temperatures are required for complex catalysts compared to three-component systems. The study concludes that while the rules guide the design of complex catalysts, their applicability to arbitrary compositions or elements with significantly different atomic radii remains unverified.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study describes a solvent-free mechanochemical method to synthesize potassium calcium phosphates from eggshell waste and KH2PO4 for soil conditioning. The process utilizes mechanical energy to promote solid-state reactions, forming phases like K3CaH(PO4)2 and CaKPO4. These products offer improved nutrient management by releasing potassium and forming hydroxyapatite at acidic soil pH levels.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study addresses the 'lab-to-fab gap' in organic solar cells by using slot-die coating with a green solvent to manufacture flexible PM6:Y6 devices. Power conversion efficiencies of 6.3% and 7.2% were achieved for binary and ternary devices, respectively. The text highlights the advantages of slot-die coating over spin-coating for scalable, roll-to-roll production.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates the impact of slot-die coating temperature on the performance of PM6:Y6 organic solar cells, finding that 100 °C yields optimal efficiency. Thermal annealing improves devices coated at lower temperatures but does not benefit those coated at higher temperatures.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study identifies trap-assisted recombination as a dominant loss mechanism in open-air processed PM6:Y6 solar cells due to impurities and interface defects. Introducing PC61BM as a ternary component enhances electron mobility and creates an energy cascade that boosts short-circuit current and overall efficiency. The optimal ternary blend ratios tested were [1:1:0.2] and [1:1.1:0.1], with the latter achieving a slightly higher average power conversion efficiency due to improved fill factor.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study reports that the atmospheric pressure continuous process achieves the best overall conversion for methane oxidation to methanol and acetic acid compared to high-pressure batch processes. The catalyst, AuFeHS, was synthesized via a modified deposition precipitation method on hydrophobic silica, which facilitates peroxide interaction and methanol desorption. Characterization confirmed atomic dispersion of iron and the presence of small gold nanoparticles (1.3-3.0 nm) with a specific surface area of 392 m²/g.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study presents a workflow to identify viable crystal structures for cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO) by filtering overlapping lithium atoms and symmetry duplicates before applying machine learning for energetic ordering. The authors note that c-LLZO has the best interfacial stability against metallic lithium among popular solid electrolytes but is not stable at room temperature without dopants. The methodology aims to resolve disagreements in the literature regarding the ground state configuration and Li site occupancy of c-LLZO.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study addresses the lack of consensus on the lithium occupancy in cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO) by generating and ranking all possible site occupancies. A brute-force approach is deemed unviable due to the vast number of combinations, so a geometric constraint of a minimum Li-Li distance of 1.7 Å is applied to eliminate overlapping atoms. This constraint limits the feasible 24d:96h site ratios, specifically restricting the 96h sites to a maximum occupancy of 48 due to their paired geometry.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study describes a workflow to generate and filter crystal structures for cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 by enforcing minimum Li-Li distances and removing symmetry duplicates. Local sensitive hashing is used to efficiently identify unique structures, reducing the dataset to approximately 2 million unique conformations. DFT calculations on subsets of these structures are used to train a multiple linear regression model for energetic ordering.

The model achieved a correlation of 0.9996 on the test set, identifying four low-energy structures with an 8:48 24d:96h ratio within 0.026 eV of the ground state.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The authors developed a fast evaluation procedure to generate and energetically order crystallographically predicted structures for crystals with partially occupied sites. They used this method to demonstrate that many existing experimental and theoretical structures for cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO) are physically infeasible due to atomic overlap. The study aims to improve accuracy and reproducibility in future computational research on this solid electrolyte.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Peptide amphiphiles and RADA-based sequences form supramolecular nanofibres that create hydrogels with tunable stiffness and biocompatibility. Mutations in RADA16, such as replacing alanine with glycine, alter fibre morphology and hydrogel mechanical properties, with A16G showing lower stiffness and thixotropy suitable for injection. These hydrogels, particularly when combined with N-cadherin, facilitate the migration of neuroblasts to injured brain sites.

knowledge_units.context_summary: GUIDEMOL is a Python-based graphical user interface for calculating molecular descriptors and 3D grid representations using RDKit. The introduction situates molecular descriptors within QSPR/QSAR methodologies and reviews existing software tools like CDK, OCHEM, and Mordred. It highlights the use of the tkinter package for building accessible interfaces for chemoinformatics users without programming skills.

knowledge_units.context_summary: GUIDEMOL is a Python-based graphical user interface for calculating molecular descriptors and 3D grid representations using RDKit. It supports both electrostatic potential and voxel-based 3D molecular encodings, which are utilized in deep learning and 3D-QSAR applications. The software is released under the BSD license and includes a command-line interface for grid calculations.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study reports the design and synthesis of cat-DHFR, a single-domain protein catenane of dihydrofolate reductase, which exhibits enhanced stability and retained catalytic function compared to its linear counterpart. The design was achieved by rewiring connectivity between secondary motifs to introduce artificial entanglement, synthesized via post-translational processing in cells. The results suggest that linear proteins can be converted into concatenated single-domain counterparts with preserved function and elevated stability.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study describes the design and cellular synthesis of a single-domain protein catenane of dihydrofolate reductase (cat-DHFR) by rewiring loop connectivity. The design was selected based on Gaussian linking number (GLN) analysis to maximize intertwinement while preserving the active site. The synthesis utilized orthogonal split-intein pairs and circular permutation to facilitate ring closure in E. coli.

attributes.composition: identical amino acid composition to cat-DHFR with extra N- and C-terminal amino acids

attributes.purpose: proof of topology by proteolytic digestion

knowledge_units.context_summary: Purified cat-DHFR and l-DHFR were characterized using chromatography, electrophoresis, mass spectrometry, and circular dichroism. Cat-DHFR exhibits a more compact structure and reduced secondary structure intensity compared to the linear control, while retaining a folded state. Optimization of the synthesis strategy revealed that placing split-intein pairs on opposite sides of the DHFR domain is necessary to overcome steric hindrance and achieve efficient catenane formation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study characterizes the kinetic and thermodynamic properties of cat-DHFR compared to linear DHFR, revealing reduced catalytic efficiency and substrate affinity. Isothermal titration calorimetry shows significantly higher dissociation constants for cat-DHFR with DHF and NADPH. Despite lower activity, cat-DHFR demonstrates enhanced tolerance to thermal and chemical denaturation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study introduces a robotic system for automating electrochemical kinetic analysis to overcome limitations of linearization methods in complex electrocatalysis. It investigates the mechanism of CO2 reduction to CO at cobalt and iron tetrapyrrole catalysts, revealing non-ideal kinetic behaviors such as potential-dependent reaction orders. The findings suggest that complex mechanisms, including electrolyte poisoning and mixed control, are prevalent in these immobilized metal tetrapyrrole electrocatalysts.

Electrolyte solutions with 1 mol/L ionic strength are prepared from stock solutions to achieve specific bicarbonate concentrations. knowledge_units.context_summary: The robotic system uses a common reservoir configuration where the cell body is rinsed after every ten electrolyses to prevent contamination. The cell design is a three-electrode, undivided compartment with a 10 mm diameter carbon paper working electrode, a platinum wire counter electrode, and an Ag/AgCl reference electrode. The lack of a membrane allows for gas and liquid management but introduces crosstalk, resulting in incomplete Faradaic efficiency closure and high hydrogen evolution rates.

The analysis identified voltage-dependent bicarbonate inhibition and complex CO2 order dependences across cobalt and iron phthalocyanine/porphyrin catalysts.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study presents the first direct experimental visualization of π-holes in molecules using Kelvin probe force microscopy. It explains how substituting peripheral hydrogens in polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons with more electronegative atoms creates electron-deficient cavities that alter electrostatic interactions.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text explains how electrostatic interactions, specifically quadrupole-quadrupole forces, stabilize heterodimers of benzene and hexafluorobenzene, highlighting the role of pi-holes. It notes that while pi-holes were previously only theoretically predicted or indirectly observed, Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) allows for direct visualization. The study experimentally confirms the presence of a pi-hole in 9,10-Dichlorooctafluoroanthracene (FCl-An) and its absence in anthracene (An) using KPFM and nc-AFM on a gold surface.

attributes.stabilization_mechanism: substantial stabilization due to close approach of aromatic rings

attributes.prior_status: developed exclusively on a theoretical basis using quantum calculations; existence proven only indirectly experimentally

ideal imaging tool for real space observation of pi-hole systems; previously used to resolve sigma-hole for the first time

knowledge_units.context_summary: High-resolution nc-AFM and DFT calculations resolved the supramolecular assembly of anthracene and 9,10-dichlorooctafluoroanthracene on Au(111), revealing a rhombic structure driven by electrostatic interactions. While nc-AFM images showed similar contrast for both molecules, Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) was employed to map charge distributions with atomic resolution. The study notes that KPFM contrast is highly dependent on tip-sample distance, with submolecular features emerging at shorter distances but risking artifacts from tip relaxation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study uses Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to visualize the π-hole in 9,10-dichlorooctafluoroanthracene (FCl-An) and compares its adsorption properties with anthracene (An) on Au(111). KPFM simulations using the PP-AFM code reproduce the experimental bow-tie pattern of the local contact potential difference (LCPD), which corresponds to the electrostatic potential distribution. Force-distance spectroscopy reveals that FCl-An adsorbs at a greater height (360 pm) than An (330 pm) due to suppressed charge induction caused by the π-hole.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study explains that the π-hole in FCl-An increases ionization potential, suppressing charge induction at the metal interface compared to An. SAPT0 analysis confirms that dispersion energy dominates the adsorption interaction for both molecules, while induction energy is higher for An. Experimental methods involved KPFM and nc-AFM imaging at 4.2 K on Au(111) substrates.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study introduces a machine learning force field (MLFF) approach to rank candidate solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) structures in lithium-ion batteries by predicted energy. It addresses the limitations of traditional density functional theory (DFT) methods, which are too slow for the large length and time scales of SEI formation, by leveraging the speed of classical force fields with DFT-level accuracy. The authors utilize a combination of classical sampling and a novel multitask MLFF model to generate and rank these structures for future comparison with experimental results.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates the biological activity of Ajuga iva extracts, specifically phytoecdysteroids and clerodanes, against the African cotton leafworm Spodoptera littoralis. Phytoecdysteroids are plant steroids that mimic insect molting hormones, potentially disrupting larval development and serving as a green pest control method. The research aims to evaluate the efficacy of these compounds in integrated pest management programs.

attributes.function: analogs of steroid hormones controlling molting and metamorphosis in arthropods
attributes.synthesis_pathway: mevalonic acid pathway in cytosol from phytosterols
attributes.mechanism: mimic insect 20-hydroxyecdysteroid, bind insect ecdysone receptors
attributes.effects: abnormal larval development, feeding deterrence, death
attributes.toxicity_to_mammals: not toxic due to structural difference from mammalian steroids

attributes.biosynthesis: derived from geranylgeranyl diphosphate via deoxyxylulose phosphate pathway in cytoplasm
attributes.location: mostly in leaves and stems of Lamiaceae and Asteraceae families

It demonstrates the ability to amplify the full viral genome from low copy numbers and detect mutations via next-generation sequencing.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text highlights the limitations of RT-PCR in detecting SARS-CoV-2, noting that it misses a significant portion of true positives and is hindered by sample heat inactivation. To address this, the authors propose a multiplex PCR-based method that offers higher sensitivity and specificity, capable of distinguishing SARS-CoV-2 from other respiratory pathogens and enabling full-genome sequencing for surveillance.

knowledge_units.context_summary: A mathematical model estimates that standard RT-PCR detects only 4.8 copies of SARS-CoV-2 at 95% probability, while a multiplex PCR panel of 172 primers improves this limit to 1.15 copies. The study assumes a 6% amplification efficiency for single-strand cDNA and notes that the detection limit is independent of viral genome size.

attributes.advantage: detects fragments of degraded viral nucleotide fragments and tolerates genomic variations

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study demonstrates that using two overlapping pools of multiplex PCR primers achieves a calculated detection limit of 0.29 copies of SARS-CoV-2 at 95% probability. Validation using plasmids spiked into human cDNA showed that the method can detect viral copies down to 2.8, with a dynamic range up to approximately 1,000 copies. Experimental results indicated a 56% detection probability for 1.1 copies, suggesting the actual amplification efficiency is higher than the 6% estimated in the mathematical model.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study validated the uniformity and recovery rates of multiplex PCR amplicons using plasmid standards and applied the method to 13 SARS-CoV-2 positive specimens. Sequencing depth analysis showed that high genome coverage is achievable even at low viral copy numbers, with specific thresholds for mutation detection based on allele frequency.

attributes.algorithm_requirement: detected by two independently developed algorithms

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study categorized 13 SARS-CoV-2 specimens into three groups based on mutation similarity, identifying the D614G mutation in 11 samples. Researchers applied a 20% allele frequency cutoff to distinguish true intra-host mutations from PCR and sequencing noise, noting that low viral copy numbers and read depth can introduce false positives. A multiplex-PCR-based metagenomic method using random hexamer adapters was developed to detect novel pathogens and highly mutated viruses.

attributes.historical_spread: began in Europe in early February, became dominant

attributes.purpose: characterize highly mutated viruses and discover unknown pathogens

knowledge_units.context_summary: A multiplex-PCR-based metagenomic method using random hexamers enriches viral targets from human genomic background, achieving high coverage of SARS-CoV-2 and mitochondrial regions while depleting human ribosomal RNA. The method recovers 96% of the SARS-CoV-2 genome with uniform depth, distinguishing it from standard RT-PCR by its tolerance to mutations and ability to interrogate the full genome.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates the translational accuracy of Ribo-T, a tethered ribosome with covalently linked subunits in Escherichia coli. It analyzes the ribosome's behavior in frameshifting, stop codon readthrough, and internal translation initiation. The authors conclude that covalent attachment alters the ribosome's ability to correctly initiate and terminate translation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Ribo-T ribosomes, which have covalently linked subunits, are functional but exhibit slower cell growth and reduced protein synthesis rates compared to wild-type ribosomes. The study investigates Ribo-T's translational accuracy, specifically regarding frameshifting and stop codon readthrough, finding that tethered ribosomes are impaired in +1 frameshifting and termination but otherwise comparable to wild-type ribosomes.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study utilized the pCL99 plasmid, which contains a lacZ-luc fusion gene under T7 promoter control, to assess translational accuracy. Target sequences were inserted at the MscI site between the lacZ and luc genes, with translational efficiency calculated as the ratio of luciferase to beta-galactosidase activity relative to in-frame controls. Wild-type and Ribo-T ribosomes were distinguished using specific Shine-Dalgarno (SD) sequences complementary to their respective 16S rRNAs.

In contrast, Ribo-T ribosomes show significantly reduced +1 frameshifting efficiency compared to wild-type ribosomes, even when the SD sequence is adapted for Ribo-T recognition. These findings indicate that Ribo-T ribosomes are unable to sense SD sequences to stimulate frameshifting in either direction.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates how Ribo-T ribosomes utilize Shine-Dalgarno (SD) sequences for translation initiation using a dual-reporter system. Results indicate that Ribo-T ribosomes use the SD sequence inefficiently compared to wild-type ribosomes. The data suggest that translation initiation of the downstream gene occurs via internal loading rather than 70S re-initiation from the upstream gene.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Ribo-T ribosomes exhibit reduced efficiency in utilizing SD sequences for both translation initiation and frameshifting compared to wild-type ribosomes. The covalent tethering of subunits in Ribo-T is associated with a 50% reduction in protein synthesis rate and longer doubling times in E. coli. These findings suggest that the structural constraints of Ribo-T impair standard SD-ASD interactions required for optimal translational accuracy and initiation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Statistical methods for rare variant association studies (RVAS) aggregate variants within biological units to overcome the low power of single-variant analyses. Existing approaches include burden tests, variance component tests like SKAT, and hybrid methods like SKAT-O. Bayesian models such as HBMR and MiST incorporate variant characteristics and detection errors to improve power.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text introduces BATI, a Bayesian rare variant association test using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) to overcome the computational limitations of MCMC in genome-wide scans. BATI is integrated into the rvGWAS framework, which combines quality control, filtering, and multiple association tests including Burden, SKAT-O, KBAC, MiST, and HBMR. The method demonstrates superior performance over existing tests when using prior information on protein function and handles complex population structures.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The BATI method uses Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation to efficiently estimate full Bayesian models with complex random effects, allowing the integration of variant characteristics as covariates. Model selection is performed using the difference in Deviance Information Criteria (ΔDIC), with thresholds determined via simulation to control type I error. A semi-synthetic benchmarking approach was developed by combining real whole-exome sequencing data with known risk variants from ClinVar to create realistic disease cohorts.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study presents a combined evidence approach to prioritize Nipah Virus Inhibitors (NVIs) by curating a knowledgebase of 182 compounds, including 98 small molecule inhibitors. The methodology involves computing over 1,800 descriptors, applying PAINS and DruLito filters for toxicity and drug-likeness, and evaluating assay robustness. Nipah Virus is characterized as a pleomorphic, enveloped, negative-sense single-stranded RNA virus with a case fatality rate exceeding 75%.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study analyzes 3D genome alterations and gene expression in 18 T-ALL patients and 4 controls, finding that structural changes correlate with gene regulation and subtype classification. Approximately 29% of differentially expressed genes are linked to 3D genome changes, with specific compartment switches and loop alterations driving upregulation or downregulation in distinct pathways. The CDK6 locus shows strong intra-TAD interactions and consistent upregulation across all T-ALL samples.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study identifies 46 chromosomal translocations in T-ALL samples, 34 of which are novel, leading to the formation of 44 new translocation-mediated loops. These loops often anchor at pre-existing loop anchors and CTCF binding sites, with 78% linked to convergently oriented CTCF motifs, suggesting a loop extrusion mechanism. Translocations activate T-ALL-associated transcription factors via cis-acting enhancer hijacking or trans-acting gene fusions.

knowledge_units.context_summary: ProNetView-ccRCC is an interactive web-based portal designed to visualize and explore the clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) phosphopeptide co-expression network derived from CPTAC data. The tool allows users to interact with a network of 3,614 genes and 30 functional modules, querying associations between phosphopeptide abundance and clinical variables such as tumor grade.

knowledge_units.context_summary: ProNetView-ccRCC is an open-access web portal for interactive 3D exploration of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) phosphopeptide co-expression networks. The tool visualizes a network of 20,976 phosphopeptides and 30 functional modules derived from CPTAC data using a random-forest algorithm and Glay clustering. It allows users to query genes, pathways, and clinical variables such as tumor grade and stage.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study presents a novel animal model demonstrating that primary tumor excision causes spontaneous regression of early-stage micro-metastases in triple-negative breast cancer. This regression is attributed to the removal of secreted factors from the primary tumor that support metastatic development. The research identifies specific secreted mediators whose neutralization halts metastasis progression.

The findings suggest that blocking these factors can arrest micrometastasis development, offering a potential therapeutic strategy.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study utilizes ATR-FTIR spectroscopy to monitor molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells activated by CpG DNA and LPS. Findings indicate that activation leads to increased nucleic acid, protein, and lipid concentrations, with RNA synthesis preceding DNA synthesis. The research demonstrates FTIR spectroscopy as a viable independent modality for tracking macrophage activation dynamics.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The Foster method is a novel environmental DNA sampling technique using colony entrance swabs and dual-target qPCR to detect American Foulbrood disease before visual symptoms appear. American Foulbrood is caused by Paenibacillus larvae spores, which are highly resistant and can remain infectious for over 30 years. In New Zealand, the percentage of hives reported as infected increased from 0.21% in 2015 to 0.46% in 2021, driven by rising hive numbers and less experienced beekeepers.

Traditional culture methods are slow and variable, while standard PCR often lacks specificity or fails to utilize quantitative data. The study employs a multiplex qPCR assay and a new environmental DNA sampling method to detect clinically significant AFB infections.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study evaluated P. larvae levels in nurse bees, entire baseboards, and hive entrances from quarantine apiaries in New Zealand. A specific DNA extraction protocol using beadbeating and a commercial kit was applied to bee and swab samples. The methodology aimed to compare detection levels across different hive components to assess the viability of entrance swabbing for rapid diagnosis.

attributes.incubation: 65°C for 10 minutes with manual inversion every 3 minutes

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study details the DNA extraction protocols for bee and swab samples, including beadbeating and column-based purification. It describes the creation of a synthetic DNA standard for quantification and the statistical methods used to correlate spore levels with clinical disease. The AFBduo assay demonstrated high analytical sensitivity, detecting targets down to 4 copies per 10 µL reaction.

attributes.diluent: pooled DNA sample extracted from bees free of P. larvae

attributes.formula: Spores per swab or 10 bees = 10 (Cq ftzZ-39/-3.48) x 50

increased entrance spores and the clinical signs of AFB

attributes.analytical_sensitivity: reliably detect down to 4 copies per 10 µL reaction

knowledge_units.context_summary: The AFBduo assay demonstrated high amplification efficiency and linearity for ftsZ and 16S targets, with 16S amplifying earlier due to multi-copy nature. DNA extraction from bees yielded high purity, while swab yields were too low for spectrophotometric measurement but confirmed suitable via internal controls. Three cohorts of hives were sampled to compare P. larvae levels in bees, baseboard swabs, and entrance swabs, revealing that entrance swabs could detect clinically significant infections.

attributes.quality_verification: internal control Cq's for serial dilutions

AFB levels in nurse bee samples vs entrance swabs

attributes.purpose: reduce time and costs

knowledge_units.context_summary: Statistical analysis confirmed a strong correlation between Paenibacillus larvae spore levels and clinical American Foulbrood signs, with a threshold of 565,000 spores indicating a 95% probability of infection. The study demonstrated that hive entrance swabs provide similar detection levels to whole baseboard swabs, eliminating the need to dismantle hives. Quantification relied on the single-copy ftsZ gene due to variability in the multi-copy 16S marker.

attributes.components: integrated internal control and two markers for AFB

attributes.limitation: variability in Cq difference prevents reliance for quantification

attributes.method: standard curve with quantified synthetic template diluted in AFB-negative bee DNA

attributes.advantage: removes need to dismantle and disrupt the hive

attributes.reason: similar levels of P. larvae and internal control DNA, likely due to maximum collection capacity

knowledge_units.context_summary: Entrance swab qPCR results can distinguish infected hives from non-infected ones, even when visual symptoms are absent. In some cases, high spore levels in bees without corresponding hive debris levels were attributed to the recent establishment of colonies from infected parents. The sampling method is adaptable for detecting other bee pathogens and pests for biosecurity surveillance.

attributes.initial_dna_level: similar to hives with clinical AFB signs
attributes.subsequent_status: showed clinical signs of AFB and was destroyed

attributes.hiveware_age: less than 2 weeks old at time of sampling
attributes.colony_origin: newly established from unknowingly infected parent colony

attributes.application: detection of clinically relevant AFB levels

relationships.target: biosecurity surveillance for unwanted hive pests
hive debris collected over one week

knowledge_units.context_summary: The Foster method is a rapid, one-time sampling technique that quantifies Paenibacillus larvae to assess hive disease risk. Unlike previous methods requiring hive dismantling or repeated visits, this approach allows for composite testing and early detection of clinical signs.

attributes.purpose: provides clinically significant information on AFB status

attributes.detection_history: detected from winter debris using conventional PCR

attributes.requirements: dismantling hive to sample baseboard OR repeated visits to insert/remove sampling sheets

attributes.limitation: quantification not possible

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study introduces SPOT-Contact-Single, a method for predicting protein contact maps using ESM-1b language model outputs and residual neural networks. It demonstrates significant F1-score improvements over single-sequence and evolutionary-profile-based predictors on independent test sets. The method addresses the computational intensity and data limitations of traditional evolutionary profile generation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study addresses the limitation of single-sequence contact map predictors by incorporating unsupervised features from the ESM-1b language model. It demonstrates that combining ESM-1b attention maps with one-hot encoding and SPOT-1D-Single outputs improves prediction accuracy for proteins with few homologs. The method was validated using a curated dataset derived from ProteinNet and independent test sets.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study defines three independent test sets: SPOT-2018, Neff1-2018, and CASP14-FM, to evaluate protein contact map predictors on sequentially isolated and homolog-free proteins. Input features for the neural network ensemble include one-hot encoding, SPOT-1D-Single outputs, and ESM-1b attention maps, with specific preprocessing applied to the attention maps. Performance is evaluated using standard CASP contact definitions and metrics such as F1-score, MCC, and AUC across short, medium, and long-range contacts.

It describes an ensemble of six models trained on different feature combinations, including ESM-1b attention maps and one-hot encodings. The method is compared against other predictors like SSCpred and TrRosetta, with a focus on feature importance and training strategies.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study evaluates feature combinations for protein contact map prediction, finding that ESM-1b attention maps significantly outperform one-hot encoding and SPOT-1D-Single outputs. An ensemble of six models using direct and distogram-based strategies achieved higher F1-scores than individual models. On proteins without homologs, the proposed method outperforms evolutionary-based predictors and ESM-1b.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The EcoEvoApps project aims to bridge the gap between theoretical and empirical ecology and evolutionary biology (EEB) by providing interactive tools for mathematical models. The authors identify barriers to integration, including the perceived difficulty of equation-heavy papers and a lack of pedagogical focus on theoretical models compared to statistics or programming. The paper introduces an open-source R package and website offering interactive Shiny apps to simulate fundamental EEB models.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates the signaling pathways of CCN2 in lymphatic endothelial cells, specifically its activation of ERK via integrin av and its interaction with DUSP6. CCN2 was found to upregulate lymphatic markers and factors while slightly inhibiting cell growth through enhanced ERK-DUSP6 binding. In vivo assays confirmed that CCN2 promotes lymphangiogenesis, a process negatively modulated by DUSP6.

knowledge_units.context_summary: CCN2/CTGF promotes vascular endothelial cell proliferation and tubule formation via direct binding to integrin avb3. The lymphatic system regulates tissue pressure, immune surveillance, and fat absorption, with lymphangiogenesis essential for development and tissue repair. Impairment of lymphatic function leads to edema, fibrosis, and immune defects, while abnormal LEC proliferation causes lymphangiomas and sarcomas.

knowledge_units.context_summary: CCN2 stimulation in lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) significantly increases phospho-ERK levels without altering total ERK or other MAPK pathway components like p38, JNK, or AKT. This ERK activation is partially mediated by integrin av, as its knockdown reduces phospho-ERK, whereas integrin a9 knockdown slightly increases it. CCN2 also exerts a weak growth-inhibitory effect on LECs and induces a transient, non-persistent ERK phosphorylation response.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text describes the molecular mechanisms by which CCN2 regulates ERK signaling and lymphangiogenesis in lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). It identifies DUSP6 as a key negative regulator that dephosphorylates ERK, an interaction enhanced by CCN2. In vivo assays confirm that CCN2 promotes lymphangiogenesis, characterized by increased Podoplanin-positive vessels and co-localization of phospho-ERK and DUSP6.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study suggests that DUSP6 suppresses excessive ERK activation in CCN2-treated lymphatic endothelial cells, a mechanism consistent with in vitro findings. CCN2 is linked to angiogenesis, nerve migration, and cancer progression, particularly in oral squamous cell carcinoma where it correlates with metastasis. The authors propose that the integrin av-ERK-DUSP6 pathway represents a potential therapeutic target for OSCC.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The experimental procedures detail methods for assessing cell proliferation, gene expression, and protein signaling in lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). Specific protocols include crystal violet staining for proliferation, qRT-PCR for gene expression, siRNA transfection for gene silencing, and Western blotting for protein analysis. The study utilizes recombinant rat CCN2/CTGF protein and specific reagents from various suppliers to analyze ERK signaling and receptor tyrosine kinase phosphorylation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Tumor PD-L1 does not affect primary tumor growth or initial lung colonization efficiency but promotes lung metastasis by suppressing CTL-mediated clearance. This effect requires a functioning adaptive immune system and is mediated by a third factor present in the lung metastatic niche. Single-cell RNA sequencing of lung leukocytes revealed that PD-L1 loss drives transcriptional changes specifically in myeloid cells, including enhanced antigen presentation machinery in macrophages.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study extends findings to human patients with metastatic basal cell carcinoma, showing that PD-1 blockade releases myeloid differentiation restriction and enhances interferon signaling. The discussion highlights that tumor PD-L1 (tPD-L1) does not directly suppress CTL activation but instead binds to myeloid PD-1 (mPD-1) to create an immunologically cold metastatic niche. This mechanism distinguishes tPD-L1's role in metastasis from its potential sufficiency but not necessity in primary tumor response to PD-1 blockade.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study introduces a hydrogel-supported stem cell microarray platform that integrates glycosaminoglycan-protein conjugates to analyze growth factor signaling. This approach aims to overcome the structural complexity of extracellular glycans to optimize functional glycomaterials for regenerative therapies.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Heparan sulfate (HS) polysaccharides are glycosaminoglycans that regulate growth factor signaling and are being integrated into hydrogels for tissue engineering. Previous studies used glass-based arrays to profile HS-binding proteins and observe MAPK activation in response to FGF2. The current study introduces a hydrogel-based GAG microarray platform to analyze growth factor signaling in murine embryonic stem cells.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study developed a hydrogel-based microarray platform to assess stem cell signaling by immobilizing glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) with adhesion proteins. Heparin was covalently crosslinked to gelatin within a polyacrylamide hydrogel to ensure retention and preserve growth factor binding specificity. This method allows for the multiplexed analysis of glycan structures in murine embryonic stem cells.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper proposes a bidirectional LSTM method for decoding brain states from fMRI data by utilizing both past and future temporal context. This approach eliminates the need for delay adjustments in BOLD response modeling and achieved an 18% accuracy improvement over unidirectional models using Human Connectome Project data.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study proposes a Bidirectional LSTM framework for decoding brain states from fMRI data without requiring time-delay adjustments. It utilizes working memory data from the Human Connectome Project, specifically a 2-back task involving tools, places, faces, and body parts. The method processes temporal information from both past and future instances to capture BOLD response dynamics.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study preprocesses fMRI data by regressing out motion and low-frequency signals, using cortical parcellation to create 360 region-of-interest time series. A bidirectional LSTM model is employed to classify brain states without delay adjustment, utilizing forward and backward hidden activations to capture temporal dynamics.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text details the architectural variants of Bidirectional LSTM (bi-LSTM) used for brain state decoding, specifically vector concatenation, addition, and averaging. It describes the experimental setup using 400 HCP participants, 10-fold cross-validation, and specific hyperparameters like a window size of 40 and dropout of 0.3. The model was compared against unidirectional LSTM and feed-forward networks, with class weights applied to handle imbalance.

attributes.purpose: handle class imbalance

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study compares the classification accuracy of unidirectional LSTM and bidirectional LSTM (bi-LSTM-c) models for decoding brain states from fMRI data. The bi-LSTM-c model achieved a higher accuracy of 0.84 compared to 0.66 for the unidirectional LSTM. Both models exhibited the highest misclassification rates for the 'Others' class, with specific confusion noted between 'body' and 'tools' stimuli.

attributes.description: Class with highest misclassification rate for both models

knowledge_units.context_summary: A phylogenomic study of 113 genomes from the thermophilic genera Anoxybacillus, Geobacillus, and Parageobacillus identified two main clades and proposed a new genus, Quasigeobacillus. The analysis utilized Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI), Average Amino Acid Identity (AAI), and a maximum likelihood tree of 662 orthologous core genes to resolve taxonomic relationships. The study highlights the limitations of 16S rRNA sequencing and the necessity of combining genomic metrics for accurate bacterial classification.

Core genes were identified using EDGAR 2.0 with Geobacillus thermodenitrificans NG80-2 as a reference, and phylogenetic trees were constructed using FastTree. knowledge_units.context_summary: Dephosphorylation of Ycf1 increases protease accessibility and drastically reduces ATPase activity, indicating that R-domain phosphorylation is essential for structural stability and function. The phosphorylated R-domain forms a scaffold with NBD1 and the lasso domain, stabilized by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions that bury significant surface area. An inhibitory phosphorylation site at S251 on the lasso domain is positioned to disrupt R-domain interactions via electrostatic repulsion.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study proposes a model where Ycf1 R-domain phosphorylation induces an ordered, bound state that stimulates ATPase activity, contrasting with the CFTR model of disordered release. This phosphorylation-driven association with NBD1 and the lasso domain explains the inhibitory effect of S251 phosphorylation via charge repulsion. The findings highlight the clinical relevance of mutations and drug binding sites near the R-domain/NBD1 interface in ABCC transporters.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study evaluated the impact of plant growth regulators (PGRs) and nitrogen fertilization on the growth and development of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk. Results indicated that PGRs increased germination and root dry mass, while soil nitrogen fertilization enhanced dry mass production and photoassimilate rates. The research also noted that high levels of gibberellic compounds can be uneconomical for pasture management.

knowledge_units.context_summary: A study of 235 patients at Korea University Guro Hospital compared outcomes of long versus short chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions treated with drug-eluting stents. While most clinical and angiographic outcomes were similar, the long CTO group had a significantly higher incidence of repeat PCI and target vessel revascularization.

Molecular modeling indicates compound 6h forms a stable complex with α-glucosidase involving hydrogen bonds and Trp329. The introduction highlights the rising global prevalence of diabetes and the therapeutic potential of α-glucosidase inhibitors beyond glucose control.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Acarbose inhibits specific digestive enzymes to prevent complex carbohydrate digestion, but resulting colonic bacterial fermentation causes gastrointestinal side effects that reduce patient compliance. The study aims to develop new α-glucosidase inhibitors by modifying pyridine, triazole, and pyrimidine scaffolds to overcome these side effects. The synthesis of fused pyrimidine derivatives involved reacting diphenoxy-N-cyanimidocarbonate with a starting material to form a triazole intermediate, followed by acid treatment and N-alkylation or thionation.

Compound 6h outperforms the reference drug acarbose in terms of binding energy and specific residue interactions.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study describes the preparation of an alpha-glucosidase enzyme solution and the setup for a screening assay using serial dilutions in a 96-well microplate. The experimental protocol involves incubating samples with the enzyme and substrate p-NPG, measuring absorbance at 405 nm, and using acarbose as a positive control. Molecular docking analysis was performed using the Autodock software package and the protein structure PDB 3W37.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Thapsigargin, a SERCA inhibitor, was tested for cytotoxicity and antiviral efficacy against paramyxoviruses and DNA viruses. The study found that Thapsigargin inhibits paramyxovirus replication without direct virucidal effects, and that SERCA2 overexpression rescues this inhibition. PPRV infection was shown to induce SERCA2 expression in Vero cells.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Thapsigargin treatment blocks virus-induced SERCA2 expression and specifically inhibits paramyxovirus entry and protein localization. Time-of-addition assays indicate that the inhibitor affects pre-budding stages of the viral life cycle for both NDV and PPRV. Immunofluorescence reveals that SERCA inhibition causes defective subcellular localization of viral proteins, trapping them in cytoplasmic foci rather than at the cell surface.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Thapsigargin treatment causes defective subcellular localization of viral proteins in approximately 70% of infected cells, compared to 10-30% in controls. Sequential passage of Newcastle disease virus (NDV) in the presence of Thapsigargin leads to partial resistance, whereas Peste des petits ruminants virus (PPRV) does not develop resistance. The study suggests that host-targeting agents like SERCA inhibitors impose a higher genetic barrier to resistance than direct viral targets.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates the transcriptional regulation of MIR196A by estrogen and its role as a prognostic biomarker in ER+ breast cancer. MIR196A is transcribed from two distinct genomic loci and targets genes involved in apoptosis, angiogenesis, and cell cycle progression. The research demonstrates that MIR196A expression is dynamically controlled by long-range interactions between ERα-bound enhancers and promoters.

knowledge_units.context_summary: MIR196A directly targets p27/Kip1 to influence the cell cycle and promote oncogenic features in cancer cell lines. The transcriptional regulation of miRNA genes, including MIR196A, involves promoters with specific histone marks and enhancer elements. In breast cancer, MIR196A expression correlates with HOXC genes and is regulated by oestrogen, as demonstrated by RNA polymerase II binding in MCF7 cells.

knowledge_units.context_summary: GRO-Seq and validation assays demonstrate that oestradiol specifically increases transcription of the MIR196A2 gene but not MIR196A1 in MCF7 cells. Chromatin interaction analyses reveal that MIR196A2 is regulated by long-range interactions between its promoters and two enhancers: the HOTAIR distal enhancer (HDE) and a novel MIR196A2-Enhancer (mE).

attributes.capability: assesses changes in transcription with high sensitivity

knowledge_units.context_summary: MIR196A expression patterns in breast cancer correlate with hormone receptor status and PAM50 subtypes, with high expression linked to poor survival in ER+ disease but better outcomes in triple-negative breast cancer. The gene serves as a prognostic biomarker where high expression predicts poor survival in post-menopausal ER+ patients but good survival in premenopausal patients. DNA methylation of the upstream CpG island is high in cancerous and non-malignant cell lines but low in normal mammary epithelial cells.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigated conspecific negative density-dependence (CNDD) in Quercus costaricensis seedlings in Costa Rican highland forests. Researchers found no significant effect of CNDD on survival, but identified bamboo density and herbivory as significant negative factors. The authors suggest that the lack of intraspecific density regulation contributes to the species' dominance.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Recent research indicates that common species may be less susceptible to conspecific negative density-dependence (CNDD) due to physiological traits and genetic diversity in immune response genes. In tropical montane forests, which are less diverse than lowland forests, Quercus costaricensis dominates the Talamanca range, comprising over 90% of basal stem area. The study hypothesized that this dominance results in weak CNDD regulation and a positive effect of nearby adults on seedling recruitment.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study found no significant conspecific negative density-dependence (CNDD) effect on the survival or recruitment of Quercus costaricensis seedlings, despite their high density and spatial aggregation. Instead, seedling survival was positively correlated with density, potentially due to herbivore satiation, while herbivory and Chusquea bamboo density negatively impacted survival. The lack of CNDD regulation is proposed to explain the dominance of this endemic oak in Costa Rican montane forests.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study evaluates the acute toxicity of six engineered nanoparticles and three soluble salts on Artemia sp. hatching and nauplii viability. The estimated order of toxicity for the nanoparticles is Ag > CuO > ZnO > Au > TiO2 > SiO2. The research highlights the need for specific hazard identification methodologies for nanomaterials due to their unique physicochemical properties and environmental risks.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study utilizes Artemia sp. as a model organism to assess the acute toxicity of six engineered nanoparticles on hatching rates and nauplii viability. Nanoparticles were sourced from the NANOVALID consortium or synthesized in-house and characterized using TEM and DLS. The research demonstrates a good inverse correlation between mortality in nauplii tests and hatching rates, suggesting the development of a new bioassay for nanoparticle hazard assessment.

Nanoparticle dispersion and size were analyzed in distilled and salt water, revealing flocculation in copper and zinc oxide samples. Statistical analysis confirmed a correlation between hatching inhibition and larval toxicity.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study reports that silver and copper oxide nanoparticles significantly reduce Artemia hatching rates, while other nanoparticles like gold and silicon dioxide show lower toxicity. Silver nitrate and ionic silver form are highly toxic to nauplii, with silver nanoparticles exhibiting an LC50 of approximately 10.12 mg/L. No gross morphological abnormalities were observed in hatched nauplii, although reactive oxygen species were detected in dead or trapped individuals.

Silver and copper oxide nanoparticles exhibited the highest toxicity, while silicon nanoparticles at low concentrations showed enhanced hatching compared to controls. The research utilized DCFDA and DHE staining to detect reactive oxygen species and superoxide in exposed nauplii.
